sources.title: On the existence of powerful p-values and e-values for composite hypotheses
sources.read_version: arXiv v4, 2024-12-01; author-hosted manuscript, not asserted to be the version of record
sources.metadata_verification: IMS official issue search record verifies title, authors, 52(5), 2241-2267 and DOI; author publication list corroborates. Direct DOI retrieval failed. Author PDF begins Submitted to the Annals of Statistics, so it is not labeled as the published typeset version.
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, definitions and joint atomlessness discussion; relevant sections 4.4-4.5 including Proposition 4.11 and Examples 4.12-4.16 in arXiv v4 numbering. No proof-by-proof review of all appendices. Secondary round additionally inspected section 6.1 Theorems 6.1-6.2, related finite-composite-alternative statements, and the scope discussion on extending SHINE.
known_contributions: Exact/pivotal existence and convex-geometric criteria
Simultaneous transport and SHINE constructions
Superadditivity and the asymptotic first-order question
Symmetric and multi-point Gaussian examples
Exact/pivotal existence for finite composite alternatives under joint atomlessness
sources.project_delta: Explicit finite-n Hellinger score-envelope calibration; in Section 8, one Q-independent calibrated statistic for every fixed finite-alphabet alternative with matching leading minimax adaptation cost. Neither existence against a composite alternative nor the first-order limit is new.

sources.title: Asymptotically Lossless Exact and Pivotal E-Values
sources.date_note: The retrieved arXiv abstract and HTML display 21 Aug 2026 and the manuscript says August 2026; the identifier is 2609.27923. The displayed date is recorded without inferring an announcement month from it. No priority argument depends on the exact day.
sources.read_scope: Abstract and setting; Theorem 2.2; Theorem 3.1; the binary-target construction and relevant proof in section 4; section 5 finite full-support coarsening, joint-atomlessness products, simultaneous purification and proof of the main theorem; discussion and references. Not an independent certification of every cited theorem.
known_contributions: First-order equality for the optimal exact pivotal expected log e-value
Finite-experiment majorization proof
Extension of the first-order statement beyond pairwise absolute continuity and finite KL
sources.project_delta: Quantitative finite-n Hellinger loss and explicit positive calibration kernel within the narrower finite-KL setting; no claim to first solve the first-order conjecture or to subsume its infinite-KL/support scope. Secondary Section 8 uses one statistic independent of Q; Theorem 2.2 in HC optimizes separately for specified Q and supplies no such uniform oracle-regret rate.

sources.metadata_verification: Author journal list confirms journal, year, volume, issue, pages and publisher document link; arXiv v2 reports acceptance to Transactions on Information Theory. IEEE conference record separately verifies the 2021 conference DOI.
sources.read_scope: ArXiv v2 abstract, introduction and setting; relevant section IV, especially Proposition 6 and discussion distinguishing it from Wilks' theorem. Not all proofs/appendices read.

First- and second-order error-exponent analysis
A central limit theorem for a maximized log-likelihood statistic under its regularity assumptions

sources.title: The numeraire e-variable and reverse information projection
sources.metadata_verification: IMS official issue record confirms formal journal metadata and DOI; arXiv abstract confirms authors and version history.
sources.read_scope: Abstract and introduction, including definitions, the numeraire/log-optimality characterization and effective-null/RIPr discussion; not all theorem proofs or examples read.

Reverse information projection without the older existence assumptions
Ordinary composite-null expected-log optimization

sources.title: Optimal e-variables under constraints
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction and stated constraint classes; Theorem 6.1 and section 7 discussion/limitation concerning LFD pairs. Full-HTML keyword search found no occurrence of pivotal. All omitted proofs were not read.
known_contributions: Optimize-then-constrain for privacy, quantization, boundedness and convex integral constraints
Composite extensions using least favorable distribution pairs
sources.project_delta: A simultaneous null-law constraint with an explicit positive measure correction for arbitrary fixed finite hypotheses. The broad idea of constrained e-variable optimization is prior work.

sources.title: Strong duality for the GROW criterion
sources.read_scope: Primary arXiv abstract and version/submission record only. Used as neighboring optimization background, not a full-text no-overlap certificate.
known_contributions: Strong duality for bounded GROW and REGROW criteria for arbitrary composite alternatives
Assumptions and limitations for extensions to unbounded e-variables
sources.project_delta: No new ordinary GROW/REGROW criterion or duality is claimed. The proposed new condition is full common-null-law exactness with quantitative adaptation for fixed finite nulls. This comparison is based only on the cited abstract, not a full-text exclusion proof.

sources.read_scope: Primary archive abstract and bibliographic record only. NML technical attribution is additionally corroborated by GHB2024 section 3.2 and Xie-Barron indexed author papers; no assertion of full-text reading.

sources.metadata_verification: Typeset first page verifies authors, journal volume/issue/pages; IEEE official indexed metadata verifies DOI and publication record.
sources.read_scope: Abstract and introductory discussion in the first approximately two pages, including the parametric KL-to-mixture asymptotic. The technical theorem conditions, applications and all proofs were not audited.

sources.project_delta: The dimension coefficient and information cost are not novel; the proposed extension preserves this leading learning cost under an additional complete common-null-law requirement.

sources.title: Growth-Optimal E-Variables and an extension to the multivariate Csiszár-Sanov-Chernoff Theorem
sources.read_version: arXiv v2, submitted 2024-12-24; PDF internal date 2024-12-30 recorded separately
sources.metadata_verification: Primary arXiv abstract page and PDF verify authors, title, v2 identifier and submission history. No journal publication verified.
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, sections 1.1-1.2 and section 3.2, especially equations (3.8)-(3.10): expected relative-GROW redundancy, individual-sequence regret and Shtarkov/NML construction. Section 4 asymptotic claims read from introduction only; all later proofs not audited.

sources.title: Minimax redundancy for the class of memoryless sources
sources.read_version: Author-hosted typeset paper indexed abstract; official IEEE indexed metadata and abstract
sources.metadata_verification: Official IEEE search result verifies title, volume/issue/pages and DOI. Author-hosted indexed typeset first page confirms authors and March 1997 issue.
sources.read_scope: Primary abstract and opening page as indexed, stating minimax expected relative entropy on the multinomial simplex and stronger constant asymptotics. Direct PDF retrieval returned 502; proofs not read.
known_contributions: Classical multinomial expected minimax redundancy and asymptotically optimal codes, including treatment of boundary risk.
sources.project_delta: No claim of a new d/2 log n lower-bound mechanism or constant; the minimax comparison transfers the existing learning scale to the exact-pivotal constrained class.

sources.title: A rank-based sequential test of independence
sources.read_version: arXiv v4, submitted 2024-01-25; PDF internal date 2024-01-29; journal metadata checked separately
sources.metadata_verification: Oxford official record verifies authors, December 2024 issue, pages and DOI; online publication 2024-05-14.
sources.read_scope: Abstract, introduction, sections 3.1-3.2, Proposition 1, test-martingale construction and Remark 2 on multinomial prediction/Jeffreys prior; beginning of section 3.3. Full performance proofs and appendices not audited.
known_contributions: Randomized ranks turn the composite independence null into a common iid uniform law; multinomial prediction then learns an unspecified alternative, with explicit coding and growth-optimality discussion.
sources.project_delta: The broad combination of common-law reduction and learning is already known. The proposed theorem treats arbitrary fixed finite null lists without rank structure and controls regret against their original-experiment ordinary oracle, not solely a transformed multinomial comparison.

sources.title: E-statistics, group invariance and anytime-valid testing
sources.read_version: Technical reading of arXiv v2 (2023-10-17); author-hosted published AoS PDF first page/introduction separately read
sources.metadata_verification: Author-hosted typeset published PDF first page and official IMS issue indexed record verify title, authors, volume/issue/pages and DOI; CWI institutional record corroborates.
sources.read_scope: ArXiv v2 abstract, introduction, section 2.4 oracle-relative objective, related-work discussion and selected statements in sections 3.1-3.3 including relative-GROW consequence and composite invariant hypotheses. Published PDF abstract/introduction read. Not a proof-by-proof review or arXiv-to-published byte comparison.
known_contributions: Under suitable group structure and amenability, maximal-invariant likelihood ratios are absolute and relative GROW among all e-statistics; composite invariant parameters and mixtures also discussed.
sources.project_delta: Common-null-law reduction with relative oracle optimality already exists in structured models. The new scope requires no group-orbit structure on the fixed finite null list and proves its separate logarithmic adaptation comparison.

cases.interpretation: Distinct active nulls need not give a positive second-order coefficient when they coincide Q-almost surely. This is outside full-support finite alphabets.

cases.argument: For every output event B, pivotality gives (4/5)(K(0,B)-K(1,B))=0. Thus both conditional output laws coincide and Q induces the common null law. Exactness and Jensen imply E_Q log E <= 0; E=1 attains 0.
cases.interpretation: An arbitrary point-mass alternative does not imply exact finite-n equality with the oracle.
